The PSNR in dB against the clean disks, 160 by 160 pixels, for the disks with Gaussian noise of sigma 20, 22.66 dB before the filter. The noise comes from NumPy's default_rng with seed 7 and is rounded to 8 bits. The other settings are the defaults: sym4, 3 levels and the estimated noise sigma.

| Threshold rule | T for h_1 | T for v_1 | T for d_1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| VisuShrink | 86.73 | 86.73 | 86.73 |
| BayesShrink | 51.16 | 50.32 | 171.41 |
| SureShrink | 80.93 | 80.93 | 80.93 |

The thresholds of the finest level. The estimated noise sigma is 19.25, close to the 20 that was added. VisuShrink uses one threshold for every subband, sigma sqrt(2 ln N) with N = 25600 pixels. BayesShrink gives each subband its own. Its threshold for d_1 is high, because the disks leave little signal in the finest diagonal details. SureShrink found all three finest subbands sparse, so its hybrid rule chose the universal threshold of their size, sigma sqrt(2 ln 6889).

With soft thresholding, BayesShrink gives the highest PSNR. VisuShrink keeps its large threshold on the coarsest level too, where the disks put most of their signal and the other rules use much lower thresholds. Soft thresholding also shrinks the edges it keeps, so VisuShrink blurs the most. With hard thresholding, VisuShrink gives the highest PSNR, since hard thresholding keeps the edges at full size.
